cases.name: Sherrelle Antoinette Bassett
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "To Live
I read of a man who stood to speak at the funeral of a friend. He referred to the dates on the tombstone from the beginning...to the end. He noted that first came the date of birth and spoke the following date with tears, but he said what mattered most of all was the DASH between those years.
Sherrelle spent her DASH as a believer of God. She believed and confessed the Lord Jesus Christ as her Savior during revival in 1996 at Christian Valley M.B. Church and on June 9, 1996, she was baptized. Sherrelle later begin attending church with her grandmother at Bethel M.B. Church where she sang in the youth choir. She credited her christian journey to several leaders such as: Rev. Melvin Webster, Rev. Stanford Johnson, Dr. M.C. Miller, and Rev. Barnard Luckett.
Sherrelle spent her DASH learning. She begin her education at Mid-Delta daycare center in Belzoni, Mississippi. She attended Humphreys County School District (HCSD) from Kindergarten through Jr. High School. Sherrelle was a member of various clubs and organizations while attending HCSD including the Beta Club, Student Council Association, and the 7th grade basketball team. During her 8th grade year, Sherrelle enrolled in Yazoo City School District where she later joined the volleyball team during her 10th grade year. On May 23, 2008, She was granted her high school diploma and following high school, Sherrelle enrolled in Mississippi Delta Community College.
Sherrelle spent her DASH as a worker and the life of EVERY party. After receiving her Certified Nursing Assistant certification she cared for patients in several nursing homes. Following working at the nursing homes, she was employed by several agencies (too many to count). Sherrelle lived her life full of joy, laughter and love. She never met a stranger. Her laugh was contagious and would light up EVERY room she stepped in.
To Cherish
Sherrelle spent her DASH as a loving and caring mother, daughter, sister, niece, and cousin."
